metric_definition_clarification: Character Error Rate (CER = Total Char Edits / Total Reference Chars) and Word Error Rate (WER = Total Word Edits / Total Reference Words) are Levenshtein edit distance ratios. They are NEVER accuracy percentages. When the hypothesis contains extra inserted text (e.g. facility headers, doctor metadata, or footers present on the page but missing from an incomplete reference body), the number of edit operations readily exceeds the reference length, producing CER or WER > 1.0 (e.g. 2.1245). This does not indicate negative accuracy, but rather an insertion-heavy reference-boundary mismatch.

reconciled_approach_a_full_page_text.description: All human-readable visible text rendered on the document (headers, patient metadata, clinical rows, reference intervals, footers)

historical_phase5_5_unaligned_baseline.description: Body-only reference snippet vs full-page OCR output (document-region boundary mismatch)
